title: How do I get logs off the flight controller?
summary: Use Airframe's guided USB, Bluetooth, mass-storage, direct MSP, or supported adapter workflow, with the available configuration evidence kept beside the import.
questions: Can Airframe discover and identify my Betaflight controller?
Should I use direct download, mass storage, or a supported Wi-Fi adapter?
Will the imported document include configuration evidence, and what can it restore?

blocks.text: Airframe can guide the transfer from a connected Betaflight flight controller into an Airframe document. The best route depends on the discovered transport and storage—not the Bluetooth device's marketing name, however confident it sounds.

items.title: Connect and select
items.text: Start Import from Flight Controller, choose USB or Bluetooth, and select the controller. Bluetooth compatibility is established from the discovered GATT layout plus a successful Betaflight MSP handshake.

items.title: Review identity and storage
items.text: Airframe reads controller identity, firmware/API context, and available dataflash information before offering import modes.

items.title: Choose an offered mode
items.text: Direct MSP works through the active MSP connection. Mass Storage is offered only where a host USB path can exist. A recognized SpeedyBee adapter can offer its supported Wi-Fi flow instead.

items.title: Import logs and available configuration
items.text: Airframe downloads or copies logs, validates candidates, retains readable segments around bounded corruption, and captures supported configuration evidence when the transport permits it.

items.title: Save the document
items.text: Complete the import into a regular .airframe file. Open Overview to verify source, segments, quality, storage context, and configuration provenance.

blocks.caption: Modes are capability-driven and only appear when supported
rows: The controller exposes readable dataflash over the current USB or Bluetooth MSP link.
Bluetooth throughput can be slow; keep the controller powered and nearby.
The controller can expose onboard flash or an SD card as a USB volume.
A USB cable to the host is required. Bluetooth cannot prove that cable is attached.
A recognized external SpeedyBee adapter provides its download protocol.
The external adapter has no host USB path, so Mass Storage is not offered through it.
The log already exists on disk as .bbl or .bfl.
This bypasses live configuration capture unless it is already associated elsewhere.

blocks.title: Erase happens after a verified import
blocks.text: Deleting controller logs is a separate, explicit step. Mass-storage flash can require a guided power cycle back into MSP before erase; Airframe does not treat a successful copy as permission to casually vaporize the source.

blocks.title: Configuration capture is useful, not omniscient
blocks.text: The current segmented capture can preserve and replay covered setting and profile assignments, but it is not an exact replacement for every structural section of Betaflight dump all. Resource, timer, and DMA assignments lack a bounded read path on affected constrained Bluetooth versions. Legacy Bluetooth paths may not support configuration import at all.

blocks.title: When Bluetooth finds the board but MSP does not answer
blocks.text: Bluetooth still needs the right job in Betaflight. Assign MSP to the UART used by your Bluetooth connection and make sure it remains enabled after flashing or changing the configuration. The UART number depends on the flight controller—there is no universal setting to copy.
